title: Creole names for musical instruments
summary: Allen asks what trumpet, trombone, banjo, guitar, clarinet, sax, piano, drums, bass and violin are called in Creole; most are the same as English or French.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Let's see. I wanted to ask you the names of a few musical instruments in Creole, if you remember them, Didi. Uh, what do you call a trumpet in Creole? Trumpet. And a cornet?
Can you repeat those? Do you mind repeating every one of them three times so I can get the pronunciation down straight and get everything down straight?
Uh-huh. I see. And a trumpet, how do you say that?
Yeah, I see. That's the same as cornet?
Uh-huh. And what about a trombone?
Uh-huh. Yeah, same. But what about a banjo? Uh-huh.
Put it in all pronounced alike almost. Banjo is banjo.
Good, fine. That's three times. Uh-huh. I guess there's no French word for banjo. That's supposed to be an American instrument.
Sure, I imagine so. It's unclear.
And let's see. What are some of the other instruments? Clarinet?
En clarinet. Mm-hmm. Let's see. Uh, what about the saxophones? What do you call the different kind of saxophones?
I only know them by the name of saxophones. That's all we always call them.

Well, I think that's a French word originally. I'm not sure. I don't know. A lot of them are French words. French words. Mostly, yeah. Translated into English? Translated into English. What about piano?
En piano. En piano, en piano.

Glenny used to say that all the time. Oh, no, no, no. He said his mother could hardly speak English, and she'd say, some fellow, she's waiting not to see you. Say, can't you get another bass player? Bosses, yeah. Let's see. Let's see. What have we got now? I think we've got pretty much everything in the rhythm section, haven't we?
Yeah, I think that's all. Yeah, piano.
En violon. Again? En violon. En violon. Good. Good.
Ah. There any other ones? What about the cello?
Okay. You got some words, Judy? Mm-hmm.
